newsitem.title: FRANCE: DHL Strasbourg air cargo hub project in doubt.
newsitem.headline: DHL Strasbourg air cargo hub project in doubt.

text.p: Plans for a DHL air cargo hub in the eastern French town of Strasbourg suffered a setback on Friday when three top local officials said the noise of intensive night-time flying would be too much for residents.

"In the current state of aircraft noise-curbing technology ...intensive night-time use of (Strasbourg) Entzheim airport is unacceptable," Strasbourg mayor Catherine Trautmann and the heads of the provincial and regional elected councils said.
A spokesman for DHL Worldwide Express said the company was disappointed but had not given hopes of opening its proposed Rhine valley regional air cargo hub at Strasbourg-Entzheim.
Protesters have called a demonstration against the project on Saturday.
The local officials said in a statement that their conclusion was based on an experts' study of the project's noise and its environmental and economic impact.

The survey, commissioned by Trautmann after local protests against late night and early morning flights, is to be reviewed by the airport's environment committee next Tuesday. The final decision is up to the French Civil Aviation authority.

"Clearly we are disappointed by the councils' remarks but we don't want to say too much at this stage," DHL Aviation Business Development Manager Steven Lewis told Reuters. He said DHL would seek clarification on several points of the statement.
While environmentalists and some politicians oppose the project, it has received strong support from the Strasbourg Chamber of Commerce and many local businesses.

The express distribution group had planned initially one or two nightly flights from Strasbourg using Convair and Electra aircraft in the final quarter of this year, rising to seven flights nightly next year.
The flights would link Strasbourg with DHL European hub at Brussels and regional centres at Britain's East Midlands, Copenhagen, Nuremberg, Cologne, Bergamo and Vitoria.
The project involves investing $5 million in an initial three to four-year phase to be followed by further investment in purpose-built facilities costing $50 million around the end of the century.
Deutsche Lufthansa AG and Japan Airlines Co Ltd each hold a 25 percent stake in DHL.
